column1: # False positives on open data: the catalogue publishes identifiers, coordinates and Unix times.
# CKAN reflects a search facet into an escaped attribute (Jinja autoescape); its redirects (OIDC
# login, a dataset id to its name) carry Flask's "Redirecting..." page, which repeats the Location;
# its vendored htmx calls eval for hx-on. Upstream CKAN 2.11 code.
# Keycloak's login page, which an anonymous visit of the Portal lands on: Keycloak binds the form
# to its session code in the action URL (no hidden token), reads KC_AUTH_SESSION_HASH in its own
# script and needs SameSite=None on its cookies for the cross-site OIDC return. Our own cookie
# (__Host-jc_edge: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) is not one of them.
# Content Security Policy where a strict one cannot be written today:
# - the catalogue: CKAN 2.11's templates carry inline scripts and styles; the edge sends
#   frame-ancestors/object-src/base-uri only (parked as T-5147 in tasks/later: a nonce CSP for CKAN);
# - the Portal: default-src 'self' with style-src 'unsafe-inline' for React's style attributes;
#   anonymous, every Portal address is the edge's redirect to Keycloak's page;
# - the assistant page /{publicId}: frameable by design (embed.js on a city's site), so it
#   names no frame-ancestors and sends no X-Frame-Options; app.js shows itself only inside the
#   deployment's own origins.
# Site isolation (COEP/COOP/CORP in one id): the Portal sends COOP same-origin; COEP require-corp
# would block the cross-origin map tiles and the framed assistant, and CORP same-origin would
# refuse what the API and the catalogue publish for other sites to read (CORS, open data).

column3: (Insufficient Site Isolation Against Spectre: see the reason above)
